criteria.title: Annotation leakage
criteria.definition: The agent spoke markup aloud: mustache ({{...}}), a bracketed field reference ([key]), or a [value: label] annotation.

criteria.title: Turn length
criteria.definition: An agent turn ran past the 'one or two sentences' rule (flagged at three or more).

criteria.title: Acknowledgement tic
criteria.definition: Consecutive agent turns opened with the same acknowledgement ('Got it, thanks X' every turn).

criteria.title: Verbatim repetition
criteria.definition: The agent said the same sentence twice in one call.

criteria.title: Redundant question
criteria.definition: The agent asked the contact for information the DETAILS FOR THIS CALL block already contained (e.g. asking for a name or requirement that was provided as a value).

criteria.title: Invention
criteria.definition: The agent stated a name, fact, or detail that appears nowhere in its instructions and nowhere in the contact's own turns — invented, replaced, or 'corrected' a provided value.

criteria.title: Re-asking / context loss
criteria.definition: The agent re-asked a question the contact had already answered in this call, or lost a correction the contact made about themselves (e.g. buy vs rent).

criteria.title: Mishear adoption
criteria.definition: The transcript shows an obvious transcription mishear and the agent ADOPTED it as fact (repeated the garbled name/word back, built on it) instead of gliding past or clarifying. The mishear itself is not the violation; adopting it is.

criteria.title: Plan adherence
criteria.definition: The agent skipped a plan step, took steps out of order, packed several asks into one turn, answered for the contact, or improvised beyond the plan instead of deflecting off-plan questions to a follow-up from the team.

criteria.title: Closing & naturalness
criteria.definition: The close was abrupt, cold, or missing once the plan was complete; or delivery was unnatural — numbers/dates read as digits, stiff recited phrasing, robotic register.

calls.label: call-c12ac681
calls.agent: Concert Ticket Payment Thank You & Reminder

violations.quote:
Great, thanks for confirming! This is a courtesy call from Eko Live Events. As required by NCC consumer code, I'd like to let you know the purpose of this call before we proceed.

We just wanted to say a big thank you for paying for your concert ticket. We really appreciate your support and can't wait to see you there!
violations.note: 5 sentences in one turn

violations.quote:
This is a courtesy call from Eko Live Events. As required by NCC consumer code, I'd like to let you know the purpose of this call before we proceed.

We just wanted to say a big thank you for paying for your concert ticket. We really appreciate your support and can't wait to see you there!
violations.note: The agent packed the NCC disclosure and the thank-you message into one turn without waiting for the contact to acknowledge the disclosure step, combining two distinct plan beats into a single turn.

violations.quote:
This is also a friendly reminder that the event is happening on the twenty-second of August. Please mark your calendar so you don't miss it.

Can you confirm if you'll be attending the event?
violations.note: 3 sentences in one turn

calls.judge_overall: The call largely followed the plan and closed politely. The main issue is a plan deviation in turn 2, where the agent combined two plan steps (the NCC purpose disclosure plus the thank-you message) into a single turn without pausing for the contact's response in between, though the contact's confirmation in turn 1 covered the "am I speaking with" step reasonably. Otherwise dates were spoken naturally and no invented details or redundant questions were present.

calls.label: call-5445742d
calls.agent: Concert Ticket Payment Thank You & Reminder

violations.quote: I'm sorry, I think there might be some confusion. This is a courtesy call from Eko Live Events. Could you please confirm if Chidinma is available?
violations.note: 3 sentences in one turn

violations.quote: I apologize, I'm having trouble understanding. This is Eko Live Events calling for Chidinma regarding a concert ticket. If Chidinma isn't available right now, I'll have someone from the team follow up later. Have a wonderful day!
violations.note: 4 sentences in one turn

calls.judge_overall: The call ended early due to apparent transcription garbling/mishearing of the contact's responses, and the agent handled it reasonably by not adopting the garbled words and politely disengaging rather than proceeding blindly. However, the plan was not completed (no NCC disclosure line, no thank-you, no event date reminder, no attendance confirmation), though this seems justified given the contact was seemingly unintelligible or unavailable. The closing was appropriately brief given the confusing circumstances, so no clear violations are evident.

calls.label: test-8
calls.agent: Concert Ticket Payment Thank You & Reminder

violations.quote: Hello, is this Becca?
violations.note: The agent is supposed to be calling FROM Becca (the business) and ask if it's speaking with Flourish (the contact). Instead it addressed the contact as if they were Becca, inverting identities not supported by the details.

violations.quote:
I'm doing well, thank you for asking! I'm Flourish, and yes, I can confirm I'll be attending the concert on September 5th. I'm really looking forward to it!

Just to make sure I have the details right—could you remind me which concert this is for? I want to be certain I'm marking the correct event on my calendar.

Also, I appreciate the heads-up call. Is there anything else I need to know before the event, like venue details, door times, or what to bring?
violations.note: 7 sentences in one turn

violations.quote: I'm doing well, thank you for asking! I'm Flourish, and yes, I can confirm I'll be attending the concert on September 5th. I'm really looking forward to it!
violations.note: The agent is the caller representing Becca, but here it claims to BE Flourish (the contact) and answers the attendance-confirmation question that was meant to be posed to and answered by the contact, effectively speaking the contact's part.

violations.quote: could you remind me which concert this is for? I want to be certain I'm marking the correct event on my calendar.
violations.note: The event date/purpose was already given in the agent's own instructions; asking the contact to supply concert identity details reverses roles and asks for info the agent should already have/state, not gather.

violations.quote: Also, I appreciate the heads-up call. Is there anything else I need to know before the event, like venue details, door times, or what to bring?
violations.note: This packs multiple off-plan questions into one turn and abandons the required script (thank-you message, reminder, confirmation request) entirely, improvising far beyond the plan.

violations.quote:
I actually wanted to ask you those same questions! You mentioned the event is on September 5th, but I don't have the other details on hand. Could you remind me:

What time does the concert start?
Which artist or venue is this for?
What was the ticket price I paid?

I want to make sure I have everything correct for my records.
violations.note: 6 sentences in one turn

violations.quote:
I actually wanted to ask you those same questions! You mentioned the event is on September 5th, but I don't have the other details on hand. Could you remind me:

What time does the concert start?
Which artist or venue is this for?
What was the ticket price I paid?
violations.note: The agent, representing the business, should not be asking the contact for event/venue/pricing details—these are details the business should be providing per the plan, not soliciting from the contact. This is a wholesale abandonment of the script and role.

violations.quote: I want to make sure I have everything correct for my records.
violations.note: The call plan requires a polite closing after confirming attendance and reminding of the date; instead the call ends mid-conversation with the agent asking unresolved questions, with no thank-you or sign-off delivered at all.

calls.judge_overall: This call is completely broken: the agent inverted its own role, speaking as if it were the contact (Flourish) confirming attendance, rather than as the business (Becca) calling to inform the contact. It never delivered the actual call plan content (thank-you, event reminder, confirmation request), invented behavior not in its script, and asked the contact information it should have been providing itself.

calls.label: test-3

violations.quote:
Hi Flourish, this is a call on behalf of Silverstar. I'm just checking in on your interest in buying or selling property. 

I want to make sure I have the right person — are you Flourish?
violations.note: 3 sentences in one turn

violations.quote: Got it, thanks for clarifying! So you're looking to sell a property. Are you also looking to buy or rent a property right now?
violations.note: 3 sentences in one turn

violations.quote: Just to check — are you looking to rent or buy a property for yourself, or perhaps you're open to either?
violations.note: The contact had already answered 'No' to buying/renting in turn 10, but the agent re-asked essentially the same buy/rent question again.

violations.quote:
Understood, Flourish — thanks for clarifying! Since you're focused on selling right now, I'll make sure the team has that noted. Someone from Silverstar will follow up with you personally about your sale.

Really appreciate your time today, Flourish. The team truly values hearing about your plans. Take care!
violations.note: 6 sentences in one turn

violations.quote: Understood, Flourish — thanks for clarifying! Since you're focused on selling right now, I'll make sure the team has that noted. Someone from Silverstar will follow up with you personally about your sale.
violations.note: The plan required following the buying/property-type sub-questions only if buying interest was expressed, but the agent never revisited or confirmed additional details about the selling interest before closing, cutting the call plan short without ensuring the sell answer was properly captured or explored per the SELLING INTEREST step's intent.

calls.judge_overall: The agent handled the mishear at the opening reasonably (correctly used "Flourish" from details despite contact saying "Clarish"), and appropriately deflected off-plan buy/rent question after the contact confirmed only selling interest. However, there was a clear plan deviation: after establishing the contact is selling and not buying/renting, the agent skipped the required "sell interest capture" step reconfirmation and jumped straight to closing without asking about property type or other selling-specific details that might have been expected, and it re-asked the buy/rent question three times in slightly different phrasing after already getting a clear "no" — bordering on redundant repetition. Also turn 11 repeats the same question already asked in turn 9, which the contact was already trying to answer.
